label: Sparse plus blobless partial in a registered worktree is the lowest-risk exact cost optimization
Shallow and reference/shared modes do not independently reduce the measured dense checkout
Private-upper COW can be exact only with a new merged-root and private-Git metadata seam
Git-managed move semantics are retained by registered worktrees, not arbitrary COW, sandbox, or virtual views
Exact attribution requires private mutable filesystem and Git status/index ownership plus path-consistent child process and detector views
Repository dependency closure and physical-path identity are independent of whether bytes are copied, sparse, or copy-on-write
Six-lane baseline is 16.5 seconds without worktrees versus 149.7 seconds with worktrees, with 1.6 GB checked-out files per tree and shared objects
The safest first experiment is sparse plus blobless partial inside registered worktrees; COW remains a separately measured runtime feature

direction: shallow or reference/shared modes as standalone checkout-cost reductions
reason: They reduce history or object storage, while the dense working-tree component remains.

direction: one physical checkout with environment-only write redirection
reason: Explicit git -C roots, redirector stripping, shared cwd cases, and report-only checkout watch prevent exact attribution.

direction: unregistered COW or sandbox views for Git move semantics
reason: Git move/repair operates on registered worktree state; arbitrary mounts require an external relocation protocol.
